title: The prayer of seeking guidance
hook: two units and a du'a when deciding (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, duha, and your line: the forenoon prayer. Did you find your two minutes somewhere between breakfast and lunch? Today, a prayer for when you can't decide. Day one thousand eighty-four.

Two job offers sit in two browser tabs. Or it's a lease, or a move back home, or a person a family has suggested, or whether to say yes to a surgery. A list of pros and cons has been written twice and torn up once. Friends have given opinions, and the opinions cancel out. A companion of the Prophet named Jabir said the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught them a prayer for exactly this, and taught it in all their affairs, the way he taught them a surah of the Qur'an. Not only the huge decisions. All of them. Today's word is that prayer.
screen: `TWO OFFERS, TWO TABS.` → `THE LIST TORN UP ONCE.` → `TAUGHT LIKE A SURAH.`

segments.voice: Istikharah means asking to be chosen for: asking God to choose the good. First, the form, from the hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari. When one of you is concerned about a matter, the Prophet said, pray two units that are not the obligatory prayer, then make this du'a. Two units, then words. Second, the words themselves, described rather than recited here. The person asks God to choose for them by His knowledge, and to give them ability by His power, because God has power and they have none, God knows and they do not. Then comes the heart of it. If this matter, and here the person names it, is good for me in my religion, my living and the way my affairs turn out, decree it for me and make it easy. If it is bad for me in those things, turn it away from me, and turn me away from it. Then decree the good for me wherever it is, and make me content with it. Notice that last part. It doesn't only ask for the right door. It asks to be at peace with whichever door opens. Third, what the hadith does not say. It mentions no dream, no sign in the sky, no rush of certainty. Scholars have described the answer in different ways. Some say you go ahead with what you were leaning toward and watch whether the way is made easy or blocked. Some speak of the heart settling. Some advise pairing it with asking people you trust. Fourth, why anyone would hand a choice over. Pickthall's translation of surah two puts it plainly: "it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you, and it may happen that ye love a thing which is bad for you. Allah knoweth, ye know not." Istikharah doesn't stop the person from deciding. It changes who they're deciding with.
screen: `TWO UNITS, THEN WORDS.` · `IF IT'S GOOD, MAKE IT EASY.` · `NO DREAM IS PROMISED.` · `YE KNOW NOT.` · then, large: `MAKE ME CONTENT WITH IT.`

segments.voice: The practice is to pray it for a decision. For now, settle, and bring one real choice to mind, big or small. Hold the first option for a few breaths. Notice your shoulders, your jaw, your stomach. Then hold the second. Don't decide anything yet. If you pray, you can pray two units today and make the istikharah du'a in the words the hadith gives, learned from a teacher or a trusted book. If you don't, you can simply sit with the choice and loosen your grip on it, open to either answer. The bell holds the time.
Istikharah. Asking God to choose the good: two voluntary units, then a du'a that asks for the good and for contentment with it. Today's word.
Your line: choose for me. Today, before one decision, even a small one, pause and say those three words inside, then go ahead and decide. Day one thousand eighty-four.

howItsDone: Muslims facing a decision pray two voluntary units and then recite the istikharah du'a taught in Sahih al-Bukhari, naming the matter in it; then they go ahead, often after asking advice from people they trust.

fork.setup: you've prayed istikharah about a move. no dream, no sign. what does the hadith tell you to wait for?
options: nothing: it promises no sign at all.
a stranger to tell you the answer.
fork.reveal: the hadith gives the prayer and the du'a, and promises no sign. some scholars say go ahead and see whether the way is made easy.

original.note: Arabic: seeking the good choice, asking God to choose. it shares its root with khayr, good.

trapdoor: what you thought: a prayer for a sign, or a dream with the answer.
what it means: two voluntary units and a du'a that hands a choice to God's knowledge.
what a scholar hears: it asks not only that the bad be turned away, but that the heart be turned from it too, and made content.
recall: strike, blow, wipe face and hands

sources.quoted: it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you, and it may happen that ye love a thing which is bad for you. Allah knoweth, ye know not.

notes: The istikharah du'a (Bukhari 1162; also 6382, 7390) is described in paraphrase only, not recited, so no new prayer wording is presented as the du'a. Confirm the paraphrase is faithful.
Pickthall 2:216 quoted from memory (mid-verse, after 'Warfare is ordained for you...'); confirm wording. The war context of the verse is not mentioned; Keeper may want it noted.
The three scholarly views on how the answer comes (proceed and see if eased; the heart settling; pairing with consultation) are summarized without names; confirm fair.
Original note: root kh-y-r shared with khayr; confirm.
The fork's 'a dream within three nights' is a distractor, not a claim.
